svg.title: Autopolyploidy and allopolyploidy
svg.desc: Conceptual, unscaled comparison. Each diploid parent has four single chromosomes: two long blue rods and two short red rods. Dark colors identify species A; light colors identify species B. The autotetraploid contains two complete diploid A genomes, eight rods. The allotetraploid contains one complete diploid A genome and one complete diploid B genome, eight rods. Rods are unreplicated chromosomes; their narrowed waists represent centromeres.
